text: Loading into Snowflake and transforming with dbt both work fine run by hand. Driftwood needs them to run automatically, in the right order, every day -- with a failure in one step actually stopping the next from running on bad data.

The driftwood_daily_elt DAG runs at 6 AM daily, so leadership can open the dashboard by 9. It validates the billing load, loads billing and usage events, then calls dbt run and dbt test as separate tasks.
Airflow's real Graph view shows exactly this kind of chained, multi-task pipeline -- each box a task, each line a dependency Airflow enforces automatically.
The actual dependency line is one operator: validate_billing_load runs first, then both loads in parallel since neither depends on the other, then dbt_run, then dbt_test.

The validation task runs first, as its own step, so a malformed export fails loudly right there -- not three tasks later as a confusing error. Both loads must finish before dbt_run starts, because the intermediate model joins billing and usage together; running dbt against only half the day's data would produce a wrong, quietly-wrong join, not a loud error.
Airflow's Grid view gives the at-a-glance run history across days -- exactly where you'd look first if someone reports a number looks off.
And when a specific task actually needs investigating, its real log output is one click away -- the same Logs tab a production on-call engineer opens.
Next lesson: connecting Power BI to these marts, now that they're refreshed automatically every day.
